title: One-Pot Firehall Meals
subtitle: Fewer dishes, fewer arguments, faster cleanup
description: One-pot firehall meals: jambalaya, chicken and rice, chili, and skillets that keep the crew fed and the sink empty.
intro: Cleanup drives what halls cook more than cookbooks admit. One-pot firehall meals trade a little browning glamour for dishes that fit in one sink. On busy nights, that trade is always worth it.

sections.heading: Skillet vs Dutch oven vs deep pot
paragraphs: Skillets for fast. Dutch ovens and stock pots for simmer. Pick one vessel and commit — do not migrate mid-recipe.

sections.heading: Cleanup is the real win
paragraphs: One pot means one soak. Assign washer before you start cooking — otherwise the cook owns dishes and morale drops.

practicalAdvice: Brown in the pot before liquid — always.
Deglaze with stock or water — free flavor.
Serve from the pot or one cambro — not twelve individual pans.

mealRecommendations.title: Firehall Chili
mealRecommendations.blurb: One deep pot — holds hot across the shift.

faqs.question: Where do these recipes come from?
faqs.answer: Each link goes to a full recipe on Firehall Meals — crew-sized portions, station timing, and steps written for a shared kitchen. Not home-blog scaling.

faqs.question: What if crew size or time changes tonight?
faqs.answer: Use Find a Meal with your headcount and minutes available. It pulls from the same hall-tested dinners these guides recommend.
